extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, judges, patent examiners, and intellectual property legal scholars (focus: Korean Patent Court precedents)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes legal standards and criteria from Korean Patent Court major decisions over two decades, covering standing, patentability (novelty, inventive step, enablement, utility), prior art, corrections, term extensions, designs and trademarks, and public-policy exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing of non-exclusive licensee to file invalidation action
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the non-exclusive licensee is an interested party who has the standing to file an invalidation action (Affirmative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the license is granted for the patent, unless there are special circumstances (e.g., the licensee is permitted to exploit the patent without restrictions as if it had acquired the patent itself, or there is no legal disadvantage such as a partnership between licensee and patentee), the licensee is in principle a person subject to legal disadvantage due to the existence of the patent right and thus has a direct and realistic interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'continuation of the previous trial' for duplicate administrative trial prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning of 'the continuation of the previous trial' in the prohibition of duplicate administrative trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'the continuation of the previous trial' as 'the decision from the previous trial is not confirmed,' not as 'the trial is continuing at IPTAB.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether well-known/common art supplements grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether well-known and commonly used art supplements grounds for rejection raised during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding publicly known arts or new grounds not notified during examination, without providing an opportunity to submit an opinion, is not considered supplementation of already-notified grounds for rejection; such additions are improper as they introduce new primary purposes inconsistent with the earlier ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: When different combination of prior art constitutes new ground for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a prior art raised in a different combinational relationship constitutes a new ground for rejection (Affirmative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if prior arts themselves were provided earlier, a newly raised ground that changes how prior arts are combined or the determination/content may be a new ground for rejection if the applicant was not given an opportunity to submit an opinion or amend in relation to that new combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time when registered utility model is publicly known
rubrics_metrics.description: Time of notice of registered utility model (i.e., date of registration as establishment of rights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration date is when the utility model is objectively perceived as disclosed to the public and the duty of confidentiality (e.g., of KIPO employees) lapses; thus after registration the utility model may be considered publicly known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of Internet posts as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of Internet posts as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difficult to determine the exact time when content was disclosed or when general public access became possible; contents may change between posting and later publication as a document, making Internet posts problematic to treat as conventional prior art without clear evidence of timing and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amending inventor-initiated disclosure purpose after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Possibility to amend the purpose of inventor-initiated disclosure after application (Affirmative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant files without intending to apply the inventor-initiated disclosure exception, submitting proof of the inventor-initiated disclosure to the patent office the day after filing can be deemed a legitimate amendment of the omitted purpose after application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a person of ordinary skill in the art (PHOSITA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning of a person of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hypothetical natural person who would have been able to obtain and understand all information at the state of the art in the relevant technical field and freely exercise ordinary means and abilities necessary for research and development available domestically and abroad at the time of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining inventive step based on an uncertain prior document
rubrics_metrics.description: How to determine inventive step of an invention based on a proposed prior document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prior document asserts facts that are uncertain (e.g., efficacy claims), it may be difficult for PHOSITA to conclude effects from that document alone; uncertain statements should not be accepted as solid factual basis to combine with other art to deny inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considering technological development trends in inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to consider technological development when determining inventiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence showing trends of development (or absence of developments) in a field over time can prove that PHOSITA could not easily conceive a claimed feature; such trends support that an inventive step exists if the claimed solution was not foreseeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty for inventions limiting purity of a known substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether novelty is denied for an invention that merely limits the purity of a publicly known substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed purity cannot be obtained using published refinement technology and the patent discloses achieving that purity, the purity limitation may not be considered well-known or commonly used; novelty may therefore not be denied by prior art that lacks such achievable purity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for parameter/numerical-limit inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for determining inventive step of inventions defined by parameters including numerical limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive step must be determined based on the technical significance of the numerical parameter. The specification must disclose that the numerical limitation has technical significance as a means to solve a different problem and show causal relationship to unique effects, or allow PHOSITA to deduce such significance; absent this, numerical limitation may be treated under legal deduction and inventive step may be denied if no significant effect difference is shown across the range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific disclosure requirement to deny novelty of a selection invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether disclosure of prior art must be specific to deny novelty of a selection invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere listing of many possible alternatives in prior art does not necessarily specifically disclose a selected element; if the cited inventions do not specifically disclose the selected configuration or its associated problem/benefit, novelty of the selection invention may remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step determination for new crystal form inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of inventive step of a crystal form (polymorph) invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish that a crystal form invention was completed at filing, it is sufficient to describe characteristics necessary to distinguish the crystal form from others and describe specific manufacturing methods enabling reproduction; describing comparative effects is not required at filing—comparative experimental data may be used later to determine significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a manufacturing process is necessary for identifying a product invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A product invention case which describes the manufacturing process deems the process necessary to identify the structure and nature of the final product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a product claim includes a limitation 'manufactured by the method in Claim X' where method features (e.g., solvents, one-step impregnation) result in structural/compositional differences of the final product (e.g., no residual solvent), those manufacturing features become necessary elements for identifying the product and must be considered when abstracting similarities/differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable expectation of success standard for cancer-treatment use claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'reasonable expectation of success' as a criterion to determine inventive step for cancer treatment usage inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the special nature of cancer treatment development, inventive step for a cancer-treatment use is denied only when PHOSITA would have had a reasonable expectation of success of discovering the treatment from prior art, not merely a possibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step criteria for method-of-administration limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for determining inventive step when claims limit method of administration of a pharmaceutical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If method-of-administration limitations do not produce significant beneficial effects beyond what is expected in the state of the art, and are within the range of what PHOSITA would expect, the limitation belongs to the public domain and inventive step is denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding pharmacological mechanism to medical use claims (correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to allow correction that adds pharmacological mechanism in a medical-usage invention (Negative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the medical usage is already clearly specified (e.g., 'treatment use for human allergic conjunctivitis'), adding a pharmacological mechanism that does not narrow the claimed medical use is unnecessary; such addition may not qualify as correcting misrepresentation or clarifying an unclear description, and claims need not be changed because of the added mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility requirement for gene-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility as a completion requirement for gene-related inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For gene-related inventions, specific utility and substantial utility must be described as credibly as possible to meet the patentability requirement of a complete invention with industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement for gene-related chemical-substance inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enablement requirements in the specification for gene-related chemical substance inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the special nature of such inventions (often related to the human body), the specification must provide specific experimental data in a detailed and clear manner sufficient to ensure that the invention has specific and substantial utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public order and good morals exclusion (sexual aids)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an invention of sexual aids violates public order and good morals (Negative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent must be denied under Article 32 if the invention is an obscene object that depicts specific sexual parts outright or its exploitation is inevitably expected to involve perverted acts; otherwise sexual aids do not necessarily violate public order and good morals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health risk as ground to deny patent (e.g., silver in food)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a patent relating to a method (e.g., making kimchi with water containing silver ion) is an invention having risk of harming public health (Affirmative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention risks public health (e.g., long-term ingestion of silver can cause argyria, and law prohibits use of silver or silver ion in food), that risk justifies denying patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'person who invented' under Article 33(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning of the person who invented under Article 33(a) of the Patent Act—who is the inventor when trade secrets and public knowledge are combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defendant merely combines public knowledge with trade secrets borrowed from the plaintiff and only the trade secrets contribute novel/inventive aspects, the overall invention may not be attributable to the defendant as the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file rule and subordinate-concept prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether subordinate-concept prior art violates the first-to-file rule (Affirmative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior-art claim that is a subordinate concept of a later-filed claim may be treated under Article 36(1) as conflicting with the first-to-file rule, i.e., earlier subordinate concept prior art can defeat later filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing/interest to seek revocation after confirmed invalidation at administrative trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest to raise a petition for invalidation of a correction after an administrative trial decision on invalidation was confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an administrative trial decision already invalidated registration and was confirmed, the interested party's interest to seek revocation of that decision disappears and a subsequent petition seeking revocation becomes improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of revocation when correction inseparable from claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In trials on invalidation where a petition for correction is raised, the scope of revocation of the administrative trial due to inseparability of the correction (Revoked in entirety).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition for correction affects Claim 1 and subordinate claims depend on Claim 1, the correction covers subordinate claims as well; acceptance of invalidation for the main corrected claim may require revocation of the administrative decision in its entirety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'period required due to a cause attributable' for term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning of the 'period required due to a cause attributable' when calculating patent term extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to the actual period of delay attributable to the patentee's fault in obtaining permits (e.g., under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act); requires a recognized causal relationship between the patentee's fault and the delay for permit issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of invention subject to extension of duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of invention subject to extension of duration under the (old) Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considering the law's purpose and history, medicines approved for the first time that show different treatment effects and have a new structural substance may be regarded as within scope of the mandate clause for duration extension even if parts show same effects as existing licensed medicines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of novelty-loss exception on identical designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which identical designs are affected by the novelty loss exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a novelty loss exception is claimed for a design known at initial time, the exception should apply to the same designs that continue to be publicly known and are identical, not only to the initially known version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness assessment for combined marks (shape + figure + word)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctiveness of a trademark combining a dimensional shape, figure, word, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinctiveness must be determined based on the combination as a whole rather than a dimensional shape alone; a non-distinctive shape combined with a distinctive figure/word used to identify source may be recognized as distinctive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of composite trademarks (adjective + noun)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctiveness of a composite trademark consisting of an adjective and a noun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which part becomes essential (noun or adjective) is determined by comprehensively considering whole composition, which part is distinctive, relative importance for the designated goods, perception and use in trade, relative distinctiveness, degree of combination, and actual trade circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration as use of a service mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Remuneration of using a service mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of a service mark is reasonably assumed to be an act of providing services at a cost or an act accompanied by cost under the Trademark Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'substantial care' for licensee supervision under Trademark Act
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Substantial care' in cases of invalidation due to misunderstanding and confusion caused by a licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Substantial care' under Article 73(1) condition item 9 is not satisfied merely by warning against misunderstanding; it requires effective and regular supervision or reporting on the usage status of the trademark.
